partners.diseaseBName: retinal dystrophy and microvillus inclusion disease
partners.mechanism_chain: STXBP2 (HGNC:11163) —DISRUPTS→ Vesicular trafficking (GO:0051014); STX3 (HGNC:11165) —DISRUPTS→ Vesicular trafficking (GO:0051014); Vesicular trafficking (GO:0051014) —LEADS_TO→ Gastrointestinal dysfunction (HP:0002705); Vesicular trafficking (GO:0051014) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal dystrophy (HP:0000500). Loss-of-function mutations in STXBP2 and STX3 disrupt the fundamental process of vesicular trafficking. This disruption impairs the proper transport of proteins and cargo within cells, leading to cellular dysfunction in various tissues. Consequently, this manifests as distinct but related phenotypes, including gastrointestinal dysfunction (characteristic of microvillus inclusion disease) and retinal dystrophy.

partners.mechanism_chain: STXBP2 (HGNC:11462) —LEADS_TO→ Familial adenomatous polyposis 1 (MONDO:0013135); IL10RB (HGNC:5707) —DISRUPTS→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69625); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-69625) —LEADS_TO→ Inflammatory bowel disease 25 (MONDO:0012941). Loss-of-function mutations in STXBP2 lead to Familial adenomatous polyposis 1. Separately, loss-of-function mutations in IL10RB disrupt the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, which is a critical component of immune regulation and homeostasis. Dysregulation of this pathway contributes to the pathogenesis of Inflammatory bowel disease 25. The convergence is on the shared JAK-STAT signaling pathway, which is essential for both normal immune function and cellular processes relevant to both disease contexts.
